headline: Brent climbs above US$96 while Wall Street closes for Thanksgiving
paragraphs: Oil made the biggest move overnight. January Brent settled at US$96.57 a barrel on Thursday in London, up 2.1% from Wednesday’s US$94.61, then eased to US$96.09 in a delayed 5:15 am Sydney quote. ING pointed to renewed concern about Middle East supply and warned that thin holiday trading could magnify moves. There was no Thursday US settlement for WTI.

Wall Street’s stock exchanges were shut for Thanksgiving, so Wednesday’s New York closes still stand: the S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq-100 lost 0.64% to 26,046.90, while the Dow gained 0.33%. The US market reopens tonight Sydney time and closes early at 5 am Saturday. There’s no fresh US cash-market read yet on whether tech shares can hold Wednesday’s late recovery.

The ASX 200 goes into Friday from Thursday’s close of about 8,764, up 0.8% as miners and energy shares led the rebound. The ABS reported a 12.2% jump in September-quarter business investment, led by data centres. That was a local boost to the investment picture, even as US investors have been questioning what they’re paying for AI stocks.

The Australian dollar was little changed at 66.30 US cents at 4:03 am Sydney, slightly below Thursday evening’s 66.35. Kitco’s spot gold bid was US$3,567.30 a troy ounce at 5:53 am, still down about 0.6% against its prior reference despite a small recovery from Thursday evening. ING linked the broader pressure on gold to expectations that US rates would stay high.
